A rule that keeps learning

Start from a rule written by hand, then let it learn.

  • The rule: “red if it's inside the middle square”. It's written by hand as a tiny network, so it's right from the start.
  • Then it learns: every time you place a point, the browser trains that network on your points, 16 rounds, like any network.
  • Try: put red dots in the middle square and blue dots around: 100% right away. Then add red dots just to the right of the square: the red area grows to take them in. Click From random to start without the rule, and it learns much worse.

How it works (for the curious)

How it trains

StepCSS, per point p and hidden unit k
forwardh = max(0, calc(x·a + y·b + c)), s = calc(Σ v·h + d)
lossg = t · clamp(0, 57 − t·s, 1): the point's colour if it's wrong or within the margin
through the ReLUf = clamp(0, h, 1), the derivative [z > 0]
updatev += Σ g·h / 31, a += v · Σ g·f·x / 151, b += v · Σ g·f·y / 151, c += v · Σ 2·g·f / 31, d += 4·Σ g, each clamped

Integers throughout. Every divisor is odd, so CSS's rounding matches Python's exactly, and the clamps keep every sum under 2²⁴. The first layer's step is five times smaller than the rest: with a big step a box edge overshoots, flips, and its ReLU dies.

The browser test places the demo sets from handwired/scripts/unfrozen.py from both starts and checks all 17 numbers at every epoch, and every error count, against the numpy reference in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
